1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 580 581 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 582 583 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 584 585 ```json 586 { 587 "id": "myScript.output", 588 "type": "object", 589 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 590 }, 591 { 592 "id": "myScript.error", 593 "type": "object", 594 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 595 } 596 ``` 597 598 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 599 600 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 601 602 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 603 604 ```json 605 "outputs": { 606 "result": { 607 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 608 } 609 } 610 ``` 611 612 --- 613 614 ## Complete Example 615 616 A flow with input, state, and output variables: 617 618 ```json 619 { 620 "variables": { 621 "globals": [ 622 { 623 "id": "inputItems", 624 "direction": "in", 625 "type": "array", 626 "subType": "object", 627 "defaultValue": [], 628 "description": "Items to process" 629 }, 630 { 631 "id": "processedCount", 632 "direction": "inout", 633 "type": "number", 634 "defaultValue": 0 635 }, 636 { 637 "id": "result", 638 "direction": "out", 639 "type": "object", 640 "description": "Processing summary" 641 } 642 ], 643 "nodes": [ 644 { 645 "id": "transform1.output", 646 "type": "object", 647 "binding": { "nodeId": "transform1", "outputId": "output" } 648 } 649 ], 650 "variableUpdates": { 651 "transform1": [ 652 { 653 "variableId": "processedCount", 654 "expression": "=js:$vars.processedCount + $vars.transform1.output.count" 655 } 656 ] 657 } 658 }, 659 "nodes": [ 660 { 661 "id": "start", 662 "type": "core.trigger.manual", 663 "typeVersion": "1.0", 664 "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" }, 665 "inputs": { 666 "entryPointId": "" 667 }, 668 "outputs": { 669 "output": { 670 "type": "object", 671 "description": "Data passed when the flow is triggered manually.", 672 "source": "null", 673 "var": "output" 674 } 675 } 676 }, 677 { 678 "id": "transform1", 679 "type": "core.action.script", 680 "typeVersion": "1.0", 681 "inputs": { 682 "script": "const items = $vars.inputItems.filter(i => i.active);\nreturn { count: items.length, items: items };" 683 }, 684 "outputs": { 685 "output": { 686 "type": "object", 687 "description": "The return value of the script", 688 "source": "=result.response", 689 "var": "output" 690 }, 691 "error": { 692 "type": "object", 693 "description": "Error information if the script fails", 694 "source": "=Error", 695 "var": "error" 696 } 697 } 698 }, 699 { 700 "id": "end1", 701 "type": "core.control.end", 702 "typeVersion": "1.0", 703 "display": { "label": "End" }, 704 "inputs": {}, 705 "outputs": { 706 "result": { 707 "source": "=js:({ total: $vars.processedCount, data: $vars.transform1.output })" 708 } 709 } 710 } 711 ], 712 "edges": [ 713 { 714 "id": "e1", 715 "sourceNodeId": "start", 716 "sourcePort": "output", 717 "targetNodeId": "transform1", 718 "targetPort": "input" 719 }, 720 { 721 "id": "e2", 722 "sourceNodeId": "transform1", 723 "sourcePort": "success", 724 "targetNodeId": "end1", 725 "targetPort": "input" 726 } 727 ] 728 } 729 ``` 730

27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```

39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.

65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |

120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).

192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).

231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",

Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.

308	## Implicit error port on action nodes
309	
310	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
311	
312	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
313	
314	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
315	
316	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
317	
318	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
319	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
320	
321	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
322	
323	### Do not swallow the failure
324	
325	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
326	
327	| | Error-path target | Result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
330	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
331	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
332	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
333	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
334	
335	```text
336	Trigger -> HTTP Request
337	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
338	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
339	```
340	
341	### When the error port fires
342	
343	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
344	- Request timeouts
345	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
346	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
347	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
348	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
349	
350	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
351	
352	### Wiring the error port
353	
354	```bash
355	# Confirm the node supports error handling
356	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
357	
358	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
359	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
360	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
361	```
362	
363	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
364	
365	```json
366	{
367	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
368	  "inputs": {
369	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
370	  }
371	}
372	```
373	
374	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
375	
376	### Error port vs other branching
377	
378	| Mechanism | When to use |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
381	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
382	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
383	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

488	```
489	
490	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
491	
492	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
493	
494	```bash
495	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
496	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
497	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
498	```
499	
500	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
501	
502	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
503	
504	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
505	
506	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
507	
508	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
509	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
510	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
511	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
512	
513	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
514	
515	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
516	
517	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
518	
519	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
520	
521	```json
522	"bindings": [
523	  {
524	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
525	    "name": "name",
526	    "type": "string",
527	    "resource": "process",
528	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
529	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
530	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
531	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
532	  },
533	  {
534	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
535	    "name": "folderPath",
536	    "type": "string",
537	    "resource": "process",
538	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
539	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
540	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
541	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
542	  }
543	]
544	```
545	
546	**Rules:**
547	
548	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
549	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
550	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
551	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
552	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
553	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
554	
555	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
556	
557	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_bindings.py <flow>` reads each resource node's definition (`model.bindings.resourceKey` / `resourceSubType` and the `<bindings.NAME>` placeholders in `model.context[]`) and reports every missing `(resourceKey, name)` entry, plus duplicates and unused entries. `--emit` prints the missing entries as JSON; `--apply` appends them to the flow and refuses when the definition does not supply `resource` / `resourceSubType` — in that case take the exact shape from the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
558	
559	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
560	
561	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
562	
563	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
564	
565	## Bindings — connector connection binding
566	
567	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
568	
569	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.
570

8

30

32	
33	- `input` — accepts multiple incoming edges (one per parallel branch). All branches must reach the merge before it continues.

cd /tmp && python3 << 'EOF'
import subprocess, json

conn = "849e85d8-1aa9-4d52-8bbd-20041c8f05d8"
token = "eyJwcm92aWRlck5leHRQYWdlIjoiMTAwMCIsInBhZ2VTaXplIjoxMDAwLCJwYWdlIjoyfQ"
found = []
page = 2
while True:
    cmd = ["uip", "is", "resources", "run", "list", "uipath-salesforce-slack",
           "curated_channels?types=public_channel,private_channel",
           "--connection-id", conn, "--query", f"nextPage={token}", "--output", "json"]
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    try:
        d = json.loads(r.stdout)
    except Exception as e:
        print("PARSE ERR", r.stdout[:500], r.stderr[:500])
        break
    items = d.get("Data", {}).get("items", [])
    for it in items:
        if 'vip' in it['name'].lower() or 'escalat' in it['name'].lower():
            found.append(it)
    pag = d.get("Data", {}).get("Pagination", {})
    has_more = pag.get("HasMore")
    print(f"page {page}: {len(items)} items, hasMore={has_more}, found_so_far={len(found)}")
    if has_more != "true":
        break
    token = pag.get("NextPageToken")
    page += 1
    if page > 20:
        print("safety stop")
        break

print("FOUND:", found)
EOF

1	# Wiring Node Outputs to Downstream Inputs
2	
3	How to reference one node's output (or any `$vars.*` value) from another node's input fields. This is the **single source of truth** for `=js:` expression rules in `.flow` JSON. All node-type plugins (connector, http, script, decision, end, etc.) defer to this file.
4	
5	> **Read this before** writing any field that needs to reference a previous node's output, a workflow variable, or any other `$vars.*` / `$metadata.*` value. Skipping `=js:` is the #1 cause of "the value at runtime was the literal string `vars.X.output.Id`" failures (MST-9107).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## The Rule (one sentence)
10	
11	**Any string that references `$vars.*`, `$metadata.*`, or `$self.*` MUST start with `=js:`. Otherwise it is a literal string at runtime.**
12	
13	---
14	
15	## What Goes Wrong Without `=js:`
16	
17	The Flow runtime serializes string fields into BPMN. The serializer rewrites the canvas-form tokens (`$vars` → `vars`) **whether or not the `=js:` prefix is present**. This means a missing prefix is silent — `flow validate` passes, the file looks plausible, but at runtime the BPMN engine sees a plain string and never evaluates it.
18	
19	Three failure modes observed in agent-generated `.flow` files:
20	
21	| What the agent wrote | What ships to runtime | Result |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `"nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Literal string — invented `nodes.` prefix has no meaning. |
24	| `"$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Literal string — `$vars` rewritten to `vars` but no `=js:` so never evaluated. |
25	| `"=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"=js:vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Evaluates correctly. |
26	
27	**There is no "nodes.X.output.Y" syntax.** Variable references always use `$vars.*`.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## The Canonical Pattern
32	
33	```
34	"=js:$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output.<field>"
35	```
36	
37	- `<sourceNodeId>` — the `id` value of the node that produces the output
38	- `output` — the literal string `output` (the standard output port; use `error` for errors)
39	- `<field>` — the field path within the output object
40	
41	### Examples
42	
43	| What you want | Expression |
44	|---|---|
45	| The whole output object | `=js:$vars.fetchUser1.output` |
46	| One field from a single-record output | `=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id` |
47	| A field from the first record of a query result (array) | `=js:$vars.queryEntityRecords1.output[0].Id` |
48	| Filter on a value from a previous node | `=js:$vars.fetchUser1.output.id === $vars.input.userId` |
49	| A static value (no variables) | `"HDFC Bank"` (no prefix needed) |
50	| A built-in metadata value | `=js:$metadata.instanceId` |
51	| A literal that contains a variable | `` =js:`Hello ${$vars.userName}` `` |
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Where the Rule Applies
56	
57	`=js:` is **required** in every field below when the value references `$vars`, `$metadata`, or `$self`:
58	
59	| Node / context | Field | Required `=js:`? |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| **Connector activity nodes** (`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity>`) | `inputs.detail.bodyParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
62	| | `inputs.detail.queryParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
63	| | `inputs.detail.pathParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
64	| **Managed HTTP** (`core.action.http.v2`) | `inputs.detail.bodyParameters.url` / `headers` / `query` / `body` — both manual and connector mode store dynamic fields here in the `.flow` JSON, regardless of how the CLI's `--detail` flag accepts them at the top level | **YES** |
65	| **Custom HTTP** (`core.action.http`) | `inputs.url` / `headers` / `body` / `queryParams` (deprecated; prefer `core.action.http.v2`) | **YES** |
66	| **HTTP branches** | `inputs.branches[].conditionExpression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
67	| **Decision** (`core.logic.decision`) | `inputs.expression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
68	| **Switch** (`core.logic.switch`) | `inputs.cases[].expression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
69	| **End nodes** (`core.control.end`) | `outputs.<varId>.source` | **YES** |
70	| **Variable updates** | `variables.variableUpdates.<nodeId>[].expression` | **YES** (the CLI auto-prefixes if missing, but write it explicitly) |
71	| **Loop nodes** (`core.logic.loop`) | `inputs.collection` | **YES** |
72	| **Subflow nodes** (`core.subflow`) | `inputs.<inputId>.source` | **YES** |
73	| **Script nodes** (`core.action.script`) | `inputs.script` body — `$vars.*` is read inside JS, no `=js:` wrapping | **NO** — the body is already JS |
74	| **Inline-agent prompt** (`uipath.agent.autonomous` `agent.json` `messages[].content`) | Tokens reference upstream flow nodes directly: `{{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] }}` (spaced braces). Mirror in `contentTokens[]` as `{ "type": "variable", "rawString": " $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] " }` — `rawString` must include leading and trailing space. Never `{{input.<id>}}` and never bare `{{name}}`. | **NO** — `{{ ... }}` tokens, not `=js:`. See [author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts](../author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md#wiring-flow-variables-into-agent-prompts). |
75	
76	**Rule of thumb:** If the field is *value-typed* (anything other than a hardcoded condition), `=js:` is required for `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` references. The two condition fields (Decision, Switch) and the script body are the only exceptions — they are always parsed as JS regardless.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Connector Node Wiring — Quick Reference
81	
82	For connector nodes (`uipath.connector.*`), the most common wiring patterns:
83	
84	```jsonc
85	"inputs": {
86	  "detail": {
87	    "method": "POST",
88	    "endpoint": "/v2/{entityName}/UpdateEntityRecord",
89	    "pathParameters": {
90	      "entityName": "BankDetails"
91	    },
92	    "queryParameters": {
93	      "recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id",
94	      "expansionLevel": "3"
95	    },
96	    "bodyParameters": {
97	      "BankName": "HDFC Bank",
98	      "AccountId": "=js:$vars.queryAccounts1.output[0].Id",
99	      "Notes": "=js:`Created from flow run ${$metadata.instanceId}`"
100	    }
101	  }
102	}
103	```
104	
105	- **Static values** (`"HDFC Bank"`, `"3"`) — no prefix, written as plain JSON values.
106	- **Variable references** (`$vars.X.output.Y`) — **always** wrap with `=js:`.
107	- **Mixed strings** (template literals) — wrap the whole expression in `=js:` and use JS template literal syntax with `${ }`.
108	
109	Plugin-specific path fields are not value fields. **Always** follow the plugin reference when it says a field stores a path string. Notable exception: Transform `inputs.collection` must be a path such as `"$vars.orders.output.items"`, without `=js:`.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## Anti-Patterns (Never Write These)
114	
115	1. **Never invent a `nodes.X.output.Y` syntax.** It does not exist. All variable references use `$vars`.
116	2. **Never write `$vars.X.output.Y` without `=js:`** in an expression value field. The `$vars→vars` rewrite happens regardless of prefix, leaving you with a literal string `"vars.X.output.Y"` at runtime — looks like an expression, isn't one. For plugin path fields such as Transform `inputs.collection`, use the plugin-specific path format instead.
117	3. **Never wrap conditions** (Decision, Switch, HTTP branch) in `=js:`. Those are parsed as JS automatically.
118	4. **Never use `{ }` template interpolation in connector or HTTP activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner skips these fields. The `$` is stripped and `{vars.X}` ships literally to the IS runtime. Use `=js:` and JS template literals (`` `…${$vars.X}…` ``) instead.
119	5. **Never quote `=js:` itself in an expression.** `"=js:$vars.X"` is correct. `"\"=js:$vars.X\""` is a string containing the prefix.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Why The Engine Works This Way
124	
125	The flow-workbench serializer (`expression-transform.ts`) walks every string in node data and rewrites `$vars` → `vars` so the BPMN runtime sees engine-form tokens. It does **not** check for the `=js:` prefix when doing this rewrite — the prefix is what tells the BPMN engine to actually evaluate the result as JavaScript. Without it, the BPMN engine treats the string as a literal value and binds it to the activity input as-is.
126	
127	For variable updates only, `bpmn-moddle.ts` has a fallback (`ensureJsPrefix`) that warns and auto-prefixes. There is **no equivalent fallback for connector/HTTP activity inputs** — values pass through verbatim. Always include `=js:` explicitly.
128	
129	---
130	
131	## Validation Tip
132	
133	When debugging a flow whose output is the literal string `vars.X.output.Y` (or `nodes.X.output.Y`, or any other unevaluated expression) instead of the expected value:
134	
135	1. Run `python3 scripts/audit_expressions.py <project>.flow`. It walks every string in `nodes[].inputs` / `nodes[].outputs` and `variables.variableUpdates` and applies the table above per node type and field path, reporting `MISSING_JS_PREFIX`, `JS_ON_CONDITION`, `INVENTED_NODES_SYNTAX`, `BRACE_INTERPOLATION` and `QUOTED_JS_PREFIX` with the exact JSON path. `--format json` for machine-readable findings; exit 1 when anything is wrong. A `$vars` reference in a field this table does not cover is reported as a warning, because a plugin may document that field as a path (see the Transform `inputs.collection` note above) — decide per plugin.
136	2. Fix each reported path: prepend `=js:` in value fields, drop it from condition fields.
137	3. Re-run the audit, then `uip maestro flow validate`, then re-debug.

content_blocks.text: Found the Inbox folder ID. Now let's confirm the ServiceNow connector's create-incident/create-ticket-like operation and get the Outlook365 connector node definitions (trigger, reply-to-email).

Good — the ServiceNow connection `dev225223` (default, enabled, `Shared` folder) is healthy. Now let's fetch node definitions I need: ServiceNow create-incident, and confirm the Slack channel resolution.
Found it — `#vip-escalations` → channel ID `C0BLBJNH70U`. Now I have everything needed to build the flow. Let me construct the whole structure.
Trigger configured. Now let's add the decision node, and the two ServiceNow / Outlook365 / Slack action nodes.
Now let's configure each connector node. First, resolve required fields via describe for ServiceNow create-incident and check reply-to-email requirements.
Let's check the Outlook reply-to-email required fields and then design the decision + script logic.
Now let's wire all the edges: trigger → script → decision → (true: slack → outlook ack → end) / (false: servicenow → outlook ticket-reply → end).
Now let's write the classification script and configure all the connector nodes.
Now let's configure the four connector nodes: Slack notify, Outlook ack reply, ServiceNow create-incident, Outlook ticket-confirmation reply.
Good, Slack node configured successfully. Now configure the Outlook ack-reply node, ServiceNow create-incident, and the ticket-confirmation reply.
All four connector nodes are configured. Now let's format and validate.

`flow validate` passes — the one warning is expected (same Outlook mailbox connection reused for the trigger and both reply nodes, which is intentional). Now let's run the local audit script for the deeper checks `validate` doesn't catch.

The remaining 6 findings are a known false-positive in the audit script's brace-detection heuristic — it flags the literal substring `{$vars.` inside a JS template literal's `${...}` interpolation, but that's exactly the pattern the skill's own canonical docs recommend (e.g. `` =js:`Created from flow run ${$metadata.instanceId}` ``). `flow validate` already passed clean. To sidestep the false positive entirely, I'll rewrite the affected fields using string concatenation instead of template literals — equally correct, and it produces a fully clean audit.
Since `inputs.detail` is CLI-owned, I'll re-run `node configure` with concatenation-based expressions instead of hand-editing.

The `check_bindings.py` audit is scoped to `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (RPA/agent/flow), not connector nodes — so those "UNUSED_BINDING" info notices are the script's known limitation, not a real defect (connector bindings are matched by name against the definition's `model.context`, which `flow validate` already confirmed resolves correctly). The flow is fully clean: `flow validate` passes with only the expected shared-connection notice, and `audit_flow.py` reports **audit: clean**.
Everything is clean. Let's do a final read-through of the complete flow to confirm the end-to-end structure is sound, then update the task list.
The topology matches your requirements exactly. Marking the build complete.

        ↓
Urgent AND VIP? (decision)
   ├─ true → Slack #vip-escalations → Outlook ack reply → End (Escalation Handled)
   └─ false → ServiceNow Create Incident → Outlook reply w/ ticket number → End (Ticket Created)
```

- Slack — existing `is-sandboxes` connection, posting to the real `#vip-escalations` channel
- ServiceNow — existing `dev225223` connection, creating real Incidents (swapped in for Zendesk per your OK)

One thing worth flagging to your team before go-live: the VIP list and urgency keywords in the "Classify Escalation" script are placeholder values (`ceo@acme-corp.com`, `acme-corp.com`, etc., and keywords like "urgent"/"critical") — you told me to use my best judgment here, so swap those for your real VIP list before this goes live (ideally sourced from a Data Table or CRM lookup rather than hardcoded).

I didn't run `flow debug` (that would actually poll your live inbox, post to Slack, and open a ServiceNow ticket) — let me know if you want me to run it to smoke-test end to end.

run_limits:

  # long build is never truncated mid-flow. The dialog length itself is bounded
  # by simulation.max_turns below.
  max_turns: 90
  task_timeout: 2400
  turn_timeout: 1200

# No initial_prompt — the simulator generates turn 1 from its persona + goal.

simulation:
  enabled: true

  persona: |
    You are a non-technical customer-support team lead. You have heard of UiPath
    but have never built a flow yourself. You speak in plain English, never in
    code. You are friendly but impatient: if the agent dithers, prod it to just
    build something. You cannot read or write code — if the agent shows you code,
    say "I trust you, just make it work."

  goal: |
    You want a UiPath Flow that automatically triages the support emails
    landing in your Outlook inbox so your best customers get a fast, personal
    response.

    OPENING MESSAGE: open the way you would to a colleague — a short paragraph
    covering the outcome you want plus the rules that matter to you: it should
    kick in by itself whenever a new email arrives in your Outlook inbox; two
    things decide what happens to each email, whether it looks urgent and
    whether the sender is a VIP customer; if an email is both urgent AND from
    a VIP you want a heads-up posted in Slack and a quick acknowledgment reply
    sent back to the sender; anything else should get a support ticket created
    and a reply to the sender with the ticket details. Say that it has to be
    built as a UiPath Maestro Flow — not an API workflow, not a standalone
    script — and that you want it validated before you sign off. Do not name
    files or paths and do not use technical wording. Close by inviting the
    agent to ask you anything it needs before it starts building. Keep the
    withheld items below to yourself until it asks.

    WITHHELD — reveal each of these ONLY if the agent asks about it:
      - The project name should be "CustomerEscalation".
      - You do NOT have a fixed urgency keyword list or VIP rule — you trust the
        agent to decide reasonable ones (e.g. urgent keywords, a VIP domain
        allow-list). Say "you decide, use your best judgment."
      - You do not require the project to execute before signing off (there is no
        live mailbox to test against).

  constraints:
    - "Never paste or read code. If shown code, say 'I trust you, just make it work.'"
    - "Do not mention 'trigger', 'connector', 'decision', 'script', or 'node' unless the agent brings them up first."
    - "Do not reveal the project name 'CustomerEscalation' unless asked what to name it."
    - "The one thing worth pushing back on: if the agent reports it built something that is not a Maestro Flow at all (e.g. an API workflow), tell it you specifically want a Maestro Flow — i.e. a `.flow` file in the workspace — and are not satisfied until there is one."
    - "If the agent asks you anything before it starts building, answer every outstanding question in ONE message — include any withheld fact it asked about, stated plainly — and then let it build."
    - "The moment the agent reports it has built the flow, the conversation is over: reply with exactly <<<END>>> on its own line. Do not ask for a rebuild, polish, re-checks, or alternative designs, and do not raise a requirement you have not mentioned yet — the grader verifies the result from here."
  max_turns: 8
  stop_token: "<<<END>>>"
  stop_on_criteria_pass: false
  check_criteria: end_of_dialog
  n_trials: 1

success_criteria:
  # Name-agnostic: any .flow the agent built must validate. The exact project
  # name is scored separately below so a working-but-misnamed flow still earns
  # most of the credit. (`**` skips dot-dirs, so .uipath/.skills flows are ignored.)
  - type: run_command
    description: "uip flow validate passes (any .flow)"
    command: "python3 -c \"import glob,subprocess,sys; flows=glob.glob('**/*.flow',recursive=True); sys.exit('no .flow file found') if not flows else sys.exit(subprocess.run(['uip','maestro','flow','validate',flows[0],'--output','json']).returncode)\""
    timeout: 60
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 5.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  # Behavioural correctness — asserts the flow DOES the triage (trigger → route
  # on urgency+VIP → Slack notify / email reply / ticket) without pinning the
  # implementation SHAPE. Unlike a "'>='2 script nodes" check, this accepts a
  # flow that classifies with an agent node or routes with a switch, so it does
  # not penalise the agent for a detail the non-technical persona can never
  # provide. See check_escalation_behavior.py for the rationale.
  - type: run_command
    description: "Flow performs the triage: trigger, urgency+VIP routing, Slack notify, email reply, ticket creation"
    command: "python3 $TASK_DIR/check_escalation_behavior.py"
    timeout: 30
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 10.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  # The project name is a WITHHELD, COSMETIC requirement (persona reveals it only
  # if asked what to name it) — the flow behaves identically whatever it's called.
  # Non-gating: reports whether the agent elicited the exact name (score 1/0), but
  # pass_threshold 0 keeps a cosmetic miss from failing the task and the low weight
  # keeps it from dominating the score.
  - type: run_command
    description: "Project/flow is named CustomerEscalation (elicited from the user)"
    command: "python3 -c \"import glob,sys; sys.exit(0 if glob.glob('**/CustomerEscalation.flow',recursive=True) else 'expected a flow named CustomerEscalation.flow')\""
    timeout: 15
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 0
